hints: Remember that every single bond is one sigma bond, while a double bond counts as one sigma plus one pi bond.
Start by sketching ethene, C2H4, as H2C=CH2 and count its 4 C-H sigma bonds plus 1 C-C sigma bond.
Now count carefully for the other three molecules, watching the C=O double bonds, and see which totals come out as odd numbers.
walkthrough:
**Recall how to count sigma bonds**

Every single bond contains exactly one sigma bond. A double bond contains one sigma bond and one pi bond.

Rule to use:
$$\text{single bond = 1 } \sigma, \quad \text{double bond = 1 } \sigma + 1 \pi$$

**Count C2H4 and C2H5OH**

For ethene, $\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}_2$: there are 4 C-H single bonds plus 1 C-C sigma from the C=C. Total = 5, which is odd.

For ethanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$: 5 C-H + 1 C-C + 1 C-O + 1 O-H = 8 sigma bonds, which is even.

**Count CH3CHO and CH3CO2H**

For ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$: 4 C-H + 1 C-C + 1 C=O sigma = 6 sigma bonds, which is even.

For ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$: 3 C-H + 1 C-C + 1 C=O sigma + 1 C-O + 1 O-H = 7 sigma bonds, which is odd.

**Decide how many are odd**

Odd sigma counts are C2H4 (5) and CH3CO2H (7). That is 2 compounds in total.

options.A: 1 is too low. You get this if you spot only one odd case, often C2H4, but miss that ethanoic acid also has 7 sigma bonds. Both the alkene and the carboxylic acid are odd.
options.B: 2 is correct. C2H4 has 5 sigma bonds and CH3CO2H has 7 sigma bonds, both odd. C2H5OH has 8 and CH3CHO has 6, both even.
options.C: 3 is incorrect. You get this if you miscount ethanal or ethanol by one, often by counting the C=O double bond as two sigma bonds instead of one sigma plus one pi.
options.D: 4 is incorrect. This would mean all are odd, which is impossible here because ethanol with 8 sigma bonds and ethanal with 6 sigma bonds are clearly even.
